title: Marketplace co-sell SKU approval + creative pocket
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc to converge on the minimum acceptance criteria and a small creative pocket (tile copy + 3 micro-variations) for co-sell marketplace SKUs. This is a practical preflight checklist intended for quick partner pilots (beta listings) — not the full legal/enterprise launch checklist.

Context / background:
- We have several partners who want to list Redwood Dedicated SKUs in their clouds as co-sell items. Partners need a lightweight playbook they can use to get from pilot sign-off -> listing creation.
- Primary goals: shorten cycles for early co-sell tile publication, ensure basic security/compliance and billing hooks are in place, and provide ready-to-use copy that marketing & partner success can iterate on.

High-level acceptance (must-pass) for pilot listing:
1) Technical compatibility: partner environment supports required entitlements (see tech gate list below).
2) Billing sanity: SKU mapping exists and partner finance confirms trial credit path or first-bill flow.
3) Privacy & data handling: minimal data residency and KMS requirements documented and agreed.
4) Tile copy + assets: one hero tile, two alternate micro-variations (for A/B) prepared and approved by partner comms.
5) Smoke test: end-to-end creation of an account, trial check, API call, and app demo inside listing console.

Tech gate checklist (pilot scope) — quick validation items:
- API connectivity: partner can call Redwood hosted endpoints via partner-managed integration or provide a direct redirect to our hosted page.
- Auth: OAuth flow or API-key provisioning documented; SSO optional for pilot but must be scoped for GA.
- Encryption: KMS integration for payloads optional for pilot; at minimum TLS 1.2+ enforced.
- Region: ensure tile declares region availability (us-west-2, eu-west-1 etc). If partner requires local-region only, note as limitation in tile copy.
- Audit: basic logging enabled and log retention window for pilot recorded (30d default).
- Rate limits/quota: set a pilot token quota and throttle policy (recommended: 1000 tokens/min per trial tenant).
- Fallback variant: pointer to a lower-cost model variant for capacity issues (e.g., reroute to quantized v1).

Billing & SKU mapping (pilot playbook):
- SKU canonical name: Redwood Dedicated — Pilot-XX (partner-specific suffix).
- Price stubbing: for pilots, set a trial credit bucket (e.g., $500 credit or 30-day 2k token cap).
- Billing integration: verify partner can consume metering events or proxy to their marketplace metering system; create a lightweight mapping doc (CSV) with fields: internal_sku, partner_sku, trial_credit_usd, billing_policy.
- Tags to surface: free_trial, co_sell_pilot, limited_availability.

Tile copy pocket (short creative snippets) — hero + 2 micro-variations
Primary hero (60–100 chars):
- "Run Redwood inference with predictable latency — Dedicated GPU pools, enterprise SLAs."
Micro-variation A (emphasize cost predictability):
- "Dedicated inference capacity for consistent latency and predictable unit costs."
Micro-variation B (emphasize security / private deploy):
- "Isolate sensitive inference workloads with private deployments and KMS support."
Longer description (200–350 chars):
- "Redwood Inference provides a developer-first platform for running large language model inference with dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling, and routing policies for latency-sensitive apps. Ideal for partners building AI features that need predictable throughput and enterprise controls."
Call-to-action buttons (ordered preference):
- Primary: "Start free pilot"
- Secondary: "Read integration guide"
- Tertiary: "Contact partner success"

Copy guidelines + quick QA rules:
- Avoid superlatives without proof. If we say "industry-leading", link to perf report.
- Tiles must include region availability and a brief note on data residency if non-global.
- Keep hero under 100 chars; description under 350 chars.
- Ensure accessibility alt-text for hero images.

Assets checklist:
- 1x 1200x600 hero image (light and dark variants)
- 1x 200x200 square logo (partner co-brand allowed per partner agreement)
- Microcopy + CTA button text file (plain text)
- Link to integration guide (hosted on docs.redwood.ai)

Pilot telemetry and smoke tests (runbook):
- Steps: provision tenant -> provision trial credits -> run standard inference request (sample prompt) -> assert response latency and success code -> fetch usage telemetry -> assert billing event generated.
- Expected telemetry fields: tenant_id, sku_id, region, request_id, latency_ms, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out. (For pilot, telemetry sampling can be at 10%.)
- Failure modes: 401 unauthorized (auth misconfig), 429 throttled (raise quota), 5xx (runtime fallback to variant). Document triage path in JIRA-GT-758.

Partner sign-off matrix (pilot):
- Partner tech lead: confirm API + auth (sign-off)
- Partner finance: confirm SKU/trial mapping (sign-off)
- Redwood SE: run the smoke test and verify telemetry + billing events
- Go-to-market manager: approve final tile copy and asset upload

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Do we require partner NDA template updates for partner logos in tile assets? (ask legal)
- Agree on the canonical partner SKUs naming convention across AWS/Azure marketplaces — can we auto-map? (ops)
- Need a small CI job to validate tile metadata (alt text present, CTAs present, description length) — file a small task (GH PR suggested above).

Quick timeline suggestion for a 2-week pilot listing (very aggressive):
Day 1: kickoff, partner provides assets + technical contact
Day 2–4: Redwood SE runs integration + confirms auth and billing mapping
Day 5: draft tile copy in the partner console, iterate with partner comms
Day 6–7: internal smoke tests + telemetry verification
Day 8: partner review and sign-off on copy
Day 9: QA in staging marketplace console
Day 10–11: small soft-launch (canary) to limited partners/customers
Day 12–14: collect early metrics, tweak microcopy, prepare GA checklist if pilot successful

Appendix — quick snippets for partner comms (email template):
Subject: Redwood + <Partner> pilot listing — assets & next steps
Body:
Hi <partner-tech> / <partner-pm>,
Thanks for partnering — attached is the minimal asset list and quick timeline. To unblock listing we primarily need the hero image, logo, and confirmation on SKU mapping (simple CSV). We’ll run a short integration smoke test and then push the tile to your sandbox for review.
Best,
Priya (GTM)

References / links:
- Integration guide (draft): https://docs.redwood.ai/integrations/marketplace-pilot
- JIRA ticket: JIRA-GT-758
- Confluence spec: CONFLUENCE-1123
- PR to validate tile metadata: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-tiles/pull/98

End of doc — notes: this should live as a quick-start living doc in Drive; when pilot matures we’ll extract a formal playbook and machine-checkable validators.
